title: I, Plural
statement: A capital I becomes a small monument: built from a city’s vertical pressure, a witnessed face, a planet held at the chest, and flowering crossbars. Here “I” is not solitary—it is a structure of histories, habitats, and shared scale.
brief:

actions.title: I, Plural
actions.statement: A capital I becomes a small monument: built from a city’s vertical pressure, a witnessed face, a planet held at the chest, and flowering crossbars. Here “I” is not solitary—it is a structure of histories, habitats, and shared scale.

notes.note: I’ll build a figurative capital “I” as an identity totem: a narrow city spine, a grounded portrait, an Earth-like inner emblem, and botanical crossbars that imply that the self is both singular and made of inherited places, bodies, and living systems.

actions.title: I, Plural
actions.statement: A capital I becomes a small monument: built from a city’s vertical pressure, a witnessed face, a planet held at the chest, and flowering crossbars. Here “I” is not solitary—it is a structure of histories, habitats, and shared scale.

notes.note: The composition already reads clearly as a monumental “I.” I’ll refine the Earth emblem’s silhouette so it reads as a luminous inner world rather than a dark geometric patch over the figure’s face.

The central figure is strong but needs a quieter symbolic field to unify its disparate fragments. I’ll add the ancient mirror’s round face behind the portrait as a dark, reflective halo, placing it behind the figure so the globe remains the active “eye” of the work.

The finished collage reads unmistakably as a capital “I”: botanical crossbars frame a city-built spine and a seated human figure, while the Earth becomes the self’s literal center of vision. The clear silhouette, restrained palette, and layered symbolism now feel resolved.
